one_paragraph_summary: Delivered March 15, 2017 at the Vicente A. Rufino Hall in the brand-new Rufino Campus of DLSU College of Law, Fort Bonifacio, this speech by CJP opens by thanking guest speaker CJ Maria Lourdes Sereno -- 'at 50 the youngest associate justice under the 1987 Constitution; 18 of 20 years as the first woman CJ' -- for her 'heart-warming address' and kind WDR2 Preface; CJP calls her 'the real judicial game changer' with 'the time, the intellectual gravitas and the passion to transform the judiciary into the model for excellence in Asia,' expressing hope to be alive at 93 in 2030 when she retires and bequeaths 'a truly transparent, accountable, excellent, independent and trustworthy judiciary.' He adds: 'I wish my wife Leni were around so she could have been reassured that she was correct when she said Yes to me 55 years ago. I am sorry that she cannot be with us as she is indisposed.' He singles out Washington SyCip (96, still robust and humble: 'Only a Bookkeeper') and Oscar Lopez ('one word: HONOR -- he never compromises truth and ethics'). The column-writing origin story: he had a 'historical romance with newspapers' (peddled them as a student) but never dreamt of writing a column; Salonga warned 'Chief justices make history; they do not write it'; Marixi countered, 'I do not know of any retired chief justice who had been offered to write a column'; they compromised on once-weekly. Since February 11, 2007, he has written 525 columns every Sunday without fail -- despite illness, carpal tunnel of both hands, travel abroad six times a year. On February 11, 2012 (5th anniversary of his first column), Sandy texted that WDR1 ranked 3rd on Amazon's courts bestseller list behind Jeffrey Toobin and Justice Scalia. WDR2 covers 2011 to mid-2016, supervised by J.V. Rufino, with a Foreword by Dr. Raul Pangalangan (former Inquirer publisher, now ICC judge). He closes by crediting the Rufino family across two generations -- Vicente A. Rufino for helping him start his law practice, Marixi and Sandy for his opinion-writing career -- and naming the venue as the tribute made institutional.
